name: Tainted Memorandum
summary: In Coldridge Valley, Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to novice gnome warlocks. His note urges them to leave old paths behind and seek power through the dark arts.

sections.title: A Discreet Summons
sections.body: At Anvilmar, fel practitioners are neither celebrated nor widely trusted. Alamar Grimm gives the Tainted Memorandum to young gnomes who study forbidden arts. He rejects the Holy Light and ordinary weapons, pointing to Gnomeregan’s fall as proof that old ways and tinkering failed their people. Grimm sees reliance on dwarven charity as a dead end. He urges gnomes to claim undeniable power and summon minions who will obey without question, if they are to secure their own future.

faq.answer: Alamar Grimm, the gnome warlock trainer in Anvilmar, wrote the Tainted Memorandum.

The memorandum is considered tainted because it deals with forbidden warlock magic. Its title reflects the distrust and stigma around demonic and fel power in Dun Morogh, where dwarven hosts keep practitioners at arm’s length.

faq.q: What does Alamar Grimm say about Gnomeregan?
faq.answer: Alamar Grimm blames traditional arcane magic and careless tinkering for bringing gnomes close to extinction when Gnomeregan fell. He believes the dwarves see gnomes as second-class citizens, and urges warlocks to claim their own absolute power instead of waiting for Alliance help.

angles.text: As a warlock, this note introduces your training under Alamar Grimm. It frames dark summoning as a way to gain control and power.
As a gnome, you hear Grimm’s appeal to the resentment over Gnomeregan’s loss and your people’s perceived place as dependent refugees in dwarven lands.
